newsitem.title: USA: Margret Rey, creator of "Curious George" dead at 90.
newsitem.headline: Margret Rey, creator of "Curious George" dead at 90.

text.p: Margret E. Rey, who with her husband created a series of beloved children's books featuring "Curious George" the inquisitive monkey, has died at her home in Cambridge, according to her publisher. She was 90.
Rey died on Saturday from complications following a heart attack she suffered about three weeks ago, according to the statement from her publisher Boston-based Houghton Mifflin.
She and her husband, Hans Augusto Rey, created the irrepressible monkey while living in Paris in the 1930s.

Just before the German invasion in 1940, the couple left the city on bicycles "with nothing but warm coats and our manscripts tied to the baggage racks and started peddling south," she told her publisher.
Rey and her husband made their way to Portugal and then to Brazil and finally to the United States where Houghton Mifflin published the first "Curious George" book in 1941.
The couple worked on six more sequels with H.A. Rey as illustrator and she as writer over the next 25 years.
More than 20 million "Curious George" books have sold in 12 languages. H.A. Rey, who illustrated the books, died in 1977.

In addition to the seven original "Curious George" books, she created 28 other adventures for the trouble-prone but charming monkey in collaboration with Alan Shalleck. Those adventures served as the basis for a television series.

"Curious George" became an industry. Mrs. Rey oversaw a merchandising programme with more than 50 licenses for Curious George products and the character has his own bookstore in Harvard Square not far from where Rey lived.

Born in Hamburg, Germany, in 1906, Rey celebrated her 90th birthday last May by donating $1 million to the Boston Public Library Foundation to improve children's rooms in its branches. She also donated $1 million to the Beth Israel Hospital Centre for Alternative Medicine for Research.
